origin.description: This function constructs the linear transformation D that maps vech(A) to vec(A) when A is a symmetric matrix.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: a positive integer value for the order of the underlying matrix

origin.details: Let T_{i,j} be an n by n matrix with 1 in its (i, j) element and zeroes elsewhere when i equals j, and with ones at both (i, j) and (j, i) when i differs from j. These matrices are constructed by T.matrices. The transpose of D is the sum over j from 1 to n and i from j to n of u_{i,j} times the transpose of vec(T_{i,j}), where u_{i,j} is column k of the order n(n + 1)/2 identity matrix with k = (j - 1)n + i - j(j - 1)/2. The function u.vectors generates these vectors.
origin.value: An n squared by n(n + 1)/2 matrix.
origin.example: D <- D.matrix(3); A <- matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4, 3, 4, 5), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE); vecA <- vec(A); vechA <- vech(A); y <- D %*% vechA; print(y); print(vecA)

translation.description: This function constructs the linear transformation D that maps vech(A) to vec(A) when A is a symmetric matrix.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: a positive integer value for the order of the underlying matrix

translation.details: The implementation follows the matrixcalc formula using the same T matrices, u vectors, and column-major vec as R.
translation.value: An n squared by n(n + 1)/2 matrix.
translation.example:
from matrixcalc.d_matrix import d_matrix
import numpy as np
D = d_matrix(3)
A = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [2, 3, 4], [3, 4, 5]], dtype=float)
vecA = A.reshape(-1, order="F")
vechA = np.array([A[i, j] for j in range(3) for i in range(j, 3)])
y = D @ vechA
print("y:")
print(y.reshape(-1, 1))
print("vecA:")
print(vecA.reshape(-1, 1))
